67285.subject: English Language
67285.question_text:
Choose the word that has the same rhyme scheme as the following word:

battle
67285.explanation:
battle - /ˈbæt.əl/

raffle - /'ræf.əl/

latter - /'læt.ə/

bitter - /ˈbɪt.ə/

kettle - /'ket.əl/

Battle and kettle have the same rhyme scheme because they both end with the syllable /təl/.

67287.subject: English Language
67287.question_text:
The words in capital letter have the emphatic stress. Choose the options to which the given sentences relate.
I bought my WIFE a red dress
67287.explanation:
Emphatic stress is the placement of greater stress on a particular word in a phrase or sentence. In this case, the word wife is emphasized to correct a mistake that has been made in the question. To find the appropriate question to the response: I bought my WIFE a new dress, you have to find the question that has a word that is different from the emphasized word/ the word in capital letters. The correct question is

A. Did I buy my husband a new dress?

No. I bought my WIFE a new dress.

options.text: Did I buy my husband a red dress?
Did I buy my wife a red shoe?
Did he buy my wife a red dress?
Did I buy my wife a black dress?

67288.subject: English Language
67288.question_text:
This question is based on "The Life Changer" novel.

Dr. Samuel Johnson is also known as_____
67288.explanation: He is also known as Samjohn. We can find this in pg. 19 of the novel where Ummi's husband casually refers to Dr Samuel Johnson as Dr. Samjohn, his friend who had helped with Ummi's admission.

67289.subject: English Language
67289.question_text:
Choose the word that has the same CONSONANT SOUND as the one represented by the letter(s) underlined.
wash

67290.subject: English Language
67290.question_text:
In each of the following sentences, the word that resolves the emphatic stress is written in capital letters. From the options letters A to D, choose the one to which the given sentence is the appropriate answer.

Daddy plays TENNIS on Saturday afternoons
67290.explanation:
Emphatic stress is the placement of greater stress on a particular word in a phrase or sentence. In this case, the word wife is emphasized to correct a mistake that has been made in the question. To find the appropriate question to the response: Daddy plays TENNIS on Saturday afternoons, you have to find the question that has a word that is different from the emphasized word/ the word in capital letters. The correct question is:

D. Does Daddy play cricket on Saturday afternoon?

No. Daddy plays TENNIS on Saturday afternoon.

options.text: Does mummy play tennis on Saturday afternoons?
Does daddy play tennis on Sunday afternoons?
Does daddy play tennis on Saturday morning?
Does daddy play cricket on Saturday afternoon?

67291.subject: English Language
67291.question_text:
In this question, select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.

If he were here, it could be more fun.
67291.explanation: The correct answer is 'He did not show up and so the occasion lacked much fun'. The sentence 'If he were here, it could be more fun' is a hypothetical condition that implies that the person being referred to is not present, and his presence could have made the situation more enjoyable. The other options do not fully capture the essence of the sentence.

options.text: He did not show up and so the occasion lacked much fun
He was expected but did not show up to liven up the occasion
There was no fun because he was not present
He was being expected to supply more fun

67293.subject: English Language
67293.question_text:
In this question, select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.

Though he is our elected representative, he often takes a rather jaundiced view of our problems.
67293.explanation: The phrase 'jaundiced view' is an idiomatic expression that means having a cynical or sceptical view of something. It does not mean hazy, forceful or sickly. Therefore, the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence is 'He takes an unfavourable position concerning our problems'.

options.text: He takes a rather hazy view of our problems
He takes an unfavourable position concerning our problems
He takes a rather forceful view of our problems
He takes a sickly view of our problems

67294.subject: English Language
67294.question_text:
From the words lettered A to D, choose the word that has the same consonant sound(s) as the one represented by the letter(s) underlined below.

Pin
67294.explanation: The consonant sound represented by 'P' in 'Pin' is the same as in 'Pragmatic'. In English phonetics, the 'P' in 'Pin' and 'Pragmatic' is a voiceless bilabial plosive, represented as /p/.

67295.subject: English Language
67295.question_text:
Choose the appropriate stress pattern from the options.The stressed words are in capital letter(s)
Fluency
67295.explanation: In English pronunciation, stress is placed on one syllable in a word. The word 'Fluency' is pronounced with stress on the first syllable, therefore the correct stress pattern is 'FLU-en-cy'.

67296.subject: English Language
67296.question_text:
Choose the word that is opposite in meaning to the underlined word(s)
Victor played the role of a haughty prince.
67296.explanation: Haughty means arrogantly superior and disdainful. Its antonyms include modest, humble, unpretentious, unassuming, low-key and unostentatious.

67297.subject: English Language
67297.question_text:
Choose the word or group of words that is most nearly opposite in meaning to the underlined words
The gradual process of transition to civilian rule came to an _____ end.
67297.explanation: The word 'gradual' means taking place or progressing slowly or by degrees. Therefore, the word 'abrupt' which means sudden and unexpected is the opposite of 'gradual'.

67299.subject: English Language
67299.question_text:
Fill in the gap in the sentence below with the appropriate option:
Peter and Jane love each other ...... the difficulties they face.
67299.explanation: "despite" is used to join two contrasting situations in a sentence. e.g He was rich despite the difficulties he went through.

67300.subject: English Language
67300.question_text:
Choose the option that is nearest in meaning to the underlined word
I was skeptical about the story she told me.
67300.explanation: The word 'skeptical' means not easily convinced; or having doubts or reservations. Therefore, the nearest meaning to 'skeptical' among the options is 'doubtful'.

67304.subject: English Language
67304.question_text:
This question is based on "The Life Changer" novel.

_________ is the euphemism use for Cheat notes.
67304.explanation: In the context of the novel 'The Life Changer', the euphemism used for cheat notes is 'Notes of salvation'.This can be found on page 52 of the novel where Salma convinced her seat partner, Kola, during her final examination to scribble and slip her these "notes of salvation" as she had nothing to write.

67305.subject: English Language
67305.question_text:
This question is based on "The Life Changer" novel.

why did Omar say he passed his SSCE by no means a small feat?
67305.explanation: In the novel 'The Life Changer', Omar says he passed his SSCE by no means a small feat because he passed excellently on his first attempt. This can be found on page 8 of the novel. He was bragging to his sister, Teemah, about how he passed his exams excellently even when some of his colleagues paid a lot of money to some 'Miracle Centres' and still failed their exams.

options.text: because he failed other subjects but passed maths and English
because he registered with one of the miracle centers
Because he passed excellently on his first attempt

67306.subject: English Language
67306.question_text:
Choose the option that has the same vowel sound as the one represented by the letter[s] underlined.

naked
67306.explanation:
The correct answer is bid.

The 'e' in the word 'naked' is pronounced as  /ɪ/ - /ˈneɪkɪd/. Therefore the word with the same vowel sound is 'bid'.

67307.subject: English Language
67307.question_text:
From the list of words in A to D, choose one that best describes the sentence.
James and Henry were at daggers drawn when I knew them. This means that they
67307.explanation: The phrase 'at daggers drawn' is an idiom which means to be bitterly hostile or at enmity with someone. It does not literally mean that they always wore daggers or were good at drawing daggers or were fighting everybody. Therefore, the option 'were always angry with each other' best describes the sentence.

options.text: were always angry with each other

67308.subject: English Language
67308.question_text:
This question is based on "The Life Changer" novel.

Who among Salma's roommate was reserved and withdrawn yet generous to a fault?
67308.explanation: In the novel 'The Life Changer', Ngozi is described as being reserved and withdrawn yet generous to a fault. It is her generosity that leads to a strong bond between the roommates. She always shares her food with the rest and this leads them to start cooking as a small family.

67310.subject: English Language
67310.question_text:
Choose the word that has the same rhyme scheme as the word below:
Day
67310.explanation:
Rhyme scheme refers to the pattern of end sounds or words in a verse or line of poetry. In this case, we are looking for a word that rhymes with 'Day' /deɪ/

dare -  /deə/

anime  - /ˈænɪmeɪ/

flight - /flaɪt/

ball - /bɔːl/

The word day and anime end with the /eɪ/ sound, therefore, they rhyme with each other.

67311.subject: English Language
67311.question_text:
In this question, fill each gap with the most appropriate option from the list provided.

Without our relentless campaigns, we might ...... sure of victory in the race for the National Assembly.
67311.explanation: never have been is most appropriate. Because of the use of the modal "might," the form of anomalous HAVE to use is have. Then, after "have" comes the past participle "been".

67312.subject: English Language
67312.question_text:
In this question, fill each gap with the most appropriate option from the list provided.

We are all hungry; we ...... anything to eat since morning.
67312.explanation: haven't had is most appropriate. This is known as the present perfect tense which is used to show that an action has been completed (or not) as of the time of speaking.

67313.subject: English Language
67313.question_text:
In this question, fill each gap with the most appropriate option from the list provided.

To check desertification in the arid zones, ...... trees should be planted
67313.explanation: drought-resistant is most appropriate. Drought tolerance refers to the degree to which a plant is adapted to arid or drought conditions.

67314.subject: English Language
67314.question_text:
From the options lettered A-D, choose the option that is most nearly opposite in meaning to the underlined word.

My father is parsimonious.
67314.explanation: Parsimonious means to be very unwilling to spend money or use resources. The nearly opposite word is generous.

67316.subject: English Language
67316.question_text: Pick out the option with a different rhyme
67316.explanation: The word 'Growl' has a different rhyme from the other words. Rhyming words are words that have the same ending sound. In this case, 'Bore', 'Four', and 'Roar' all end with the '-ore' sound, while 'Growl' ends with the '-owl' sound.

67317.subject: English Language
67317.question_text:
The primary stress is indicated by writing the syllable on which it occurs in capital letters. From the words lettered A to D choose the one that has the correct stress.
category
67317.explanation: In English pronunciation, the word 'category' has the primary stress on the first syllable. Therefore, the correct option is 'CAT-e-go-ry'.

67318.subject: English Language
67318.question_text:
This question is based on "The Life Changer" novel.

Ummi is an Arabic word that is directly translated to mean_____
67318.explanation: In Arabic, 'Ummi' is directly translated to mean 'My mother'. This can be seen on page 3 of the novel. According to Ummi, she was named after her paternal grandmother.

67319.subject: English Language
67319.question_text:
From the words lettered A to D below, choose the word or group of words that is nearest in meaning to the underlined word as it is used in the passage.

Bisi has become an indispensable member of staff.
67319.explanation: The word 'indispensable' means something or someone that is absolutely necessary or extremely important in a particular situation. In this context, it means that Bisi is a very important member of the staff. Therefore, the word 'vital' is the closest in meaning to 'indispensable'.

67320.subject: English Language
67320.question_text:
Choose the option that has the same vowel sound as the letter(s) underlined

exist

67321.subject: English Language
67321.question_text:
This question is based on "The Life Changer" novel.

In Lafayette, before a stranger is hosted or accommodated, permission must be requested and granted by_______
67321.explanation: In the novel 'The Life Changer', in Lafayette, before a stranger is hosted or accommodated, permission must be requested and granted by the Hakimi. The Hakimi is a traditional title for a local or tribal leader in some areas of the Middle East and North Africa. This can be seen on page 20 of the novel. It is an important tradition that helps to ensure that no criminal or fugitive from justice is harboured or accommodated in the village.

67322.subject: English Language
67322.question_text: Choose the word that does not have the same vowel sound as the others
67322.explanation: The words 'sun', 'shun', and 'son' have the same vowel sound /ʌ/, while 'short' has a different vowel sound /ɔ:/. Therefore, 'short' does not have the same vowel sound as the others.

67323.subject: English Language
67323.explanation: From the passage, it is clear that Athens had interceded for the other Greek city-states against the Persian domination. This means that Athens had intervened on behalf of the other Greek city-states. Therefore, the correct answer is option 2.

67324.subject: English Language
67324.question_text: Darius took drastic steps to __________ the rebellious Athenians.
67324.explanation: In the passage, it is mentioned that 'In anger the king sent an enormous army to defeat Athens. He thought it would take drastic steps to pacify the rebellious part of the empire.' This implies that Darius, the king, took drastic steps to calm the rebellious Athenians. Therefore, the correct answer is option 3.

67325.subject: English Language
67325.explanation: In the passage, it is mentioned that 'Emboldened by this participation, Athenians were prepared to die for their city-state.' This suggests that the participation of all citizens in ruling Athens gave them the strength and courage to fight against the Persians. Therefore, the correct answer is 'gave strength'.

67326.subject: English Language
67326.question_text: The people of Delos did not want to __________ the conquest of Greece
67326.explanation: In the passage, it is mentioned that 'The frightened city of Delos refused to believe this. Not wanting to abet the conquest of Greece, they fled from their city and did not return until the Persians had left.' This suggests that the people of Delos did not want to encourage or support the conquest of Greece by the Persians. Therefore, the correct answer is 'encourage'.

67327.subject: English Language
67327.question_text: The Athenians were__________ by some soldiers who arrived at Plataea
67327.explanation: In the context of the passage, the Athenians were 'strengthened' by some soldiers who arrived at Plataea. This is because the soldiers from Plataea reinforced the Athenian troops, providing them with additional strength and support in their battle against the Persians.

67328.subject: English Language
67328.question_text:
This question is based on "The Life Changer" novel.

Salma was looking more stunning on the last day of her exams because_______

options.text: her classmates had planned to go to the beach after the exam
her classmates had organized a mini picnic to wrap up the good work
her classmates had planned a photo shoot with some lecturers

67330.subject: English Language
67330.question_text:
This question is based on "The Life Changer" novel.

Why was it a double celebration for Ummi and members of her community when she gained admission into the university?

options.text: She had given birth to Omar before her admission to the university
Her husband agreed to marry her before she went for university registration
she was the first child to leave Lafayette to the university

67331.subject: English Language
67331.explanation: This best suits because the senate has to do with the legislative arm and they are saddled with responsibility of law making.

67333.subject: English Language
67333.explanation: The context of the passage suggests that the Senate is trying to 'nullify' the executive action of the President. 'Nullify' means to make legally null and void; invalidate. The Senate, being a legislative body, does not have the power to enforce, modify, or order the executive action of the President.

67334.subject: English Language
67334.explanation: In political terminology, an "arm" is often used to refer to a branch or division within a legislative body. The National Assembly is a larger legislative body, and the Senate is a component or division within it.

67337.subject: English Language
67337.explanation: In the context of the passage, the author is discussing the potential confusion that could arise if another part of the National Assembly were to disagree with the Senate. The House of Representatives is another part of the National Assembly, making it the correct answer. The Judiciary and the Executive Council are separate branches of government and do not fit the context of the sentence.

67338.subject: English Language
67338.explanation: In the context of the passage, the Senate is being criticized for overstepping its bounds and acting as both the 'litigant' and the judge of the constitutionality of the President's actions. A 'litigant' is a party involved in a lawsuit, which fits the context better than the other options. 'Defendant' and 'plaintiff' are specific types of litigants, but the passage does not specify which role the Senate is taking on. 'Attorney' does not fit because the Senate is not representing someone in a legal matter, but rather taking on the role of a party in a lawsuit.

67339.subject: English Language
67339.explanation: In the context of the passage, the function of the Senate is to 'enact' laws. To 'enact' a law means to make it official or put it into action, which is the role of legislative bodies like the Senate. 'Create' could also work, but 'enact' is more specific to the process of passing laws. 'Compose' is more commonly used in the context of writing or creating something like a piece of music or literature, not laws. 'Annul' means to declare invalid, which is not a function of the Senate mentioned in the passage.

67340.subject: English Language
67340.explanation: In the context of the passage, the Senate does not have the authority or 'power' to control the President in the exercise of his powers. The term 'power' refers to the ability or capacity to do something or act in a particular way. The other options 'might', 'dynamism', and 'strength' do not fit into the context of the sentence.

67341.subject: English Language
67341.explanation: In the context of the passage, the President is exercising his 'executive' powers. The term 'executive' refers to the branch of government responsible for implementing, administering, and enforcing laws. The other options 'official', 'authoritative', and 'judicial' do not fit into the context of the sentence.

67342.subject: English Language
67342.explanation: In the context of the passage, the exercise of the powers of the President can be 'regulated'. This means that the actions of the President can be controlled or governed according to a system or set of rules, which is the role of the National Assembly. The other options do not fit into the context of the passage.

67343.subject: English Language
67343.explanation: In the context of the passage, the exercise of the powers of the President can be regulated by 'an Act' of the National Assembly. An Act is a law that has been officially put into effect, which fits into the context of the passage. The other options do not fit into the context of the passage.

67344.subject: English Language
67344.question_text:
Choose the word or phrase from A to D which has its meaning opposite to the underlined word or words in each sentence
She was impertinent until she met her husband.
67344.explanation: Impertinent means ' not showing proper respect'. It's antonyms include polite, courteous, respectful, deferential, well bred, well mannered and civil.

67345.subject: English Language
67345.question_text:
This question is based on "The Life Changer" novel.

According to the novel, which of these characters had a nasty experience on the account of using social media?
67345.explanation: Salim had a nasty experience using social media.

67346.subject: English Language
67346.question_text:
Choose the option that is nearest in meaning to the underlined word(s)

Repugnant rules in the society should be repealed.
67346.explanation: Repugnant means extremely distasteful. Its synonyms include abhorrent, revolting, repulsive, repellent and offensive.

67347.subject: English Language
67347.question_text:
This question is based on "The Life Changer" novel.

Bint was encouraged to take French at the primary level because _____
67347.explanation: In the novel 'The Life Changer', Bint was encouraged to take French at the primary level because her parents believed that language acquisition at an early age is relatively easy. This is based on the concept that younger children have a higher ability to absorb and learn new languages.

options.text: Her parents believed that language acquisition at an early age is relatively easy
she would want to be a French mistress when she grows up
it will be useful for her when she travels to France

67349.subject: English Language
67349.question_text:
Choose the options to which the given sentence relate.

Spain won their last friendly FOOTBALL match
67349.explanation: Emphatic stress usually emphasis contrast, thus the right option should contain a word that contrasts with the emphasized word.

options.text: Who won their last friendly football match?
Did Spain win their last competitive football match
Did Spain lose their last competitive football match
Did Spain win their last friendly basketball match?

67350.subject: English Language
67350.question_text:
Choose the option that is nearest in meaning to the underlined word
The boss is quite inflexible once he has made up his mind.
67350.explanation: The word 'inflexible' means unwilling to change or compromise. Therefore, the nearest meaning to 'inflexible' among the options is 'unyielding'.

67351.subject: English Language
67351.question_text:
From the options lettered A-D, choose the option that is most nearly opposite in meaning to the underlined word.

My mother is a shrewd businesswoman.
67351.explanation: A shrewd person is able to understand and judge a situation quickly and to use this understanding to their own advantage. The nearest opposite word is gullible.

67352.subject: English Language
67352.question_text:
In the following question, choose the option that best completes the sentence.
The guest would have arrived earlier but he was _______ in traffic.
67352.explanation: The correct phrase to use is 'held up'. 'Held up' is a phrasal verb that means to be delayed or obstructed. So, 'The guest would have arrived earlier but he was held up in traffic' is the correct sentence.

67353.subject: English Language
67353.question_text:
Choose the option that is nearest in meaning to the underlined word(s)
No one would complain if you emulate good behaviour
67353.explanation: Emulate means to match or surpass, typically by imitation. Its synonyms include imitate, copy, reproduce, mimic, mirror, echo and follow.

67354.subject: English Language
67354.question_text: He was both a writer and a politician, but he was better ........ a singer
67354.explanation: The correct preposition to use after 'better' in this context is 'as'. When comparing roles or functions, 'as' is used. For example, 'He works better as a manager than as a clerk.' Therefore, the sentence should read 'He was both a writer and a politician, but he was better as a singer.'

67355.subject: English Language
67355.question_text:
Choose the word that has the same consonant sound as the one in bracket.

Smoo[th]
67355.explanation: Brother is the correct answer. The sound present here is pronounceable from the 'TH' in 'these' /ð/ (not /d/ as in 'drug' or /θ/ as in 'thanks').

67356.subject: English Language
67356.question_text: Identify the option with a different stress pattern
67356.explanation: In this case, 'importance', 'contribute', and 'deposit' all have the stress on the second syllable. However, 'reservoir' has a different stress pattern with the stress on the third syllable, making it the correct answer.

67357.subject: English Language
67357.question_text: In each of the questions, the word in capital letters has the emphatic stress. Choose the option to which the given sentence relates.The union congratulated the ELECTED president.
67357.explanation: The correct answer is - Did the union congratulate the ousted president? The option without the emphatic word - ELECTED is the correct answer.

options.text: Did the union reject the elected president?
Did the union congratulate the elected chairman?
Did the management congratulate the elected president?
Did the union congratulate the ousted president?

67360.subject: English Language
67360.question_text:
This question is based on "The Life Changer" novel.

What appellation was given to Talle for all his amazing show of personality.
67360.explanation: He was known as the quiet one.

67361.subject: English Language
67361.question_text: In each of the questions, the word in capital letters has the emphatic stress. Choose the option to which the given sentence relates.A good description INCLUDES specific nouns.
67361.explanation: The correct answer is - Does a good description exclude specific nouns?. The option without the emphatic word - INCLUDES is the correct answer.

options.text: Does a good description exclude specific nouns?
Does a good description include specific verbs?
Does a good description include obscure nouns?
Does a poor description include specific nouns?

67362.subject: English Language
67362.question_text:
Choose the word which has the same consonant sounds as the underlined letter(s)
pleasure
67362.explanation: The underlined letter(s) in the word 'pleasure' is 's'. The consonant sound of 's' in 'pleasure' is /ʒ/ (as in 'vision'). Among the options, the word 'seizure' has the same consonant sound /ʒ/.

67403.subject: English Language
67403.question_text:
This question is based on "The Life Changer" novel.

Whose reticent nature while growing up earned him the title: "The quiet one".?
67403.explanation: Talle was regarded as the quiet one while growing

67404.subject: English Language
67404.question_text:
In this question, select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.

The solution lies in choosing between various negative alternatives.
67404.explanation: The sentence 'The solution lies in choosing between various negative alternatives' implies that the solution can be found among several unfavorable or less-than-ideal options. Therefore, the option 'The solution can be found in one of the negative options' is the correct answer.

options.text: The solution lies in choosing between the positive and negative
The solution can be found in one of the negative options
The solution is a negative one

67428.subject: English Language
67428.question_text:
In this question, the word in capital letters has the emphatic stress. Choose the option to which the given sentence relates.

EMEKA finished his homework yesterday.
67428.explanation: In the sentence, the word 'Emeka' is stressed. This means the emphasis is on 'who' did the action. Therefore, the question that relates to the sentence is 'Who finished his home work yesterday?'.

options.text: Who finished his home work yesterday?
When did Emeka finish his home work?
Did Emeka do his home work yesterday?
Was Emeka helped to do his home work?

67429.subject: English Language
67429.question_text:
Choose the option that is nearest in meaning to the underlined word(s)
After thousands of years of existing, elephants still remain extant.
67429.explanation: Extant means still in existence. It's synonyms include still existing, in existence, surviving, abiding, enduring and existent.

67432.subject: English Language
67432.question_text:
This question is based on "The Life Changer" novel.

Salma stayed at the most coveted and famous ______ hostel.

67434.subject: English Language
67434.question_text:
This question is based on "The Life Changer" novel.

Who called the attention of the district head when it was discovered that Talle buys more than he could consume from the supermarket?

67436.subject: English Language
67436.question_text: In this question, identify the word that has the stress on the first syllable.

67438.subject: English Language
67438.question_text:
In each of the following sentences, the word that receives the emphatic stress is written in capital letters . From the options lettered A to D, choose the one which the sentence is the appropriate answer.
Lambusa TOOK OFF the wig.
67438.explanation: When answering emphatic stress questions, the option that does not have the "stressed word" becomes the correct answer.

options.text: Did Lambusa take off a wig?
Did Lambusa take off a ring?

67439.subject: English Language
67439.question_text:
Choose the option opposite in meaning to the underlined word in each sentence.
During the maths test, some students got an approximate score of 20.
67439.explanation: The word 'approximate' means something that is close to the actual, but not completely accurate or exact. Therefore, the opposite of 'approximate' is 'precise', which means marked by exactness and accuracy of detail.

67440.subject: English Language
67440.question_text:
In each of the following sentences, there is one underlined word. From the list of words lettered A to D, choose the one that is most nearly opposite in meaning to the underlined word.
The test shows that the lumps are malignant.
67440.explanation:
When something is malignant, it is harmful, malevolent, injurious. The antonym (opposite) of this is benign.
N.B: Malignant is also synonymous to cancerous.

67442.subject: English Language
67442.question_text:
Choose the word that has the same rhyme scheme.

sweet
67442.explanation: The correct answer is - suite. It has the same rhyming pattern with the word - suite. Also, they are homophones.

67444.subject: English Language
67444.question_text:
The primary stress is indicated by writing the syllable on which it occurs in capital letters. From the words lettered A to D choose the one that has the correct stress.
presidency
67444.explanation: The correct stress for the word 'presidency' is 'PRE-si-den-cy'. In English, stress means pronouncing one syllable of a multisyllabic word with greater emphasis (stress) than the other syllables in the word. The primary stress in a word is the syllable that is pronounced with the most force. In the word 'presidency', the first syllable 'pre' is pronounced with the most force, hence it has the primary stress.

The abeyance of school activities last semester was a reason for concern.

Mr. Brown is often described as an astute businessman
67449.explanation: An astute person is someone who is clever and quick at seeing what to do in a particular situation. Such person can also be described as shrewd.

know they may not return from their journey into space

options.text: had a dream to expand his farm
is more envied than the astronauts

67462.explanation:

Our success are conditioned by the amount of risk we are about to take

67465.explanation:
This can be seen in paragraph 2, last sen; and paragraph 3, first sentence.
A life without ambition, spent doing nothing.

67469.subject: English Language
67469.question_text: "Rough" in the first sentence of the passage means ......
67469.explanation: In the context of the passage, when the author wishes "May your road be rough," they are not cursing but rather expressing a desire for the person to face challenges and difficulties. The word "rough" in this context means facing challenges that will ultimately lead to opportunities and growth. Therefore, the correct answer is C. challenges that will breed opportunities.

options.text: the dangers attributed to space travel

Band[a]ge
67472.explanation: The vowel /i/ as in bit is present here. Only the very last sound pronunciation of 'cacophony' bears the same answer.

67476.subject: English Language
67476.question_text:
From the options lettered A-D, choose the option that is nearest in meaning to the underlined word.
I have an aversion for war movies.
67476.explanation: The word 'aversion' refers to a strong dislike or disinclination. Therefore, the option that is nearest in meaning to 'aversion' is 'dislike'.

67479.subject: English Language
67479.question_text:
Choose the option that is nearest in meaning to the underlined word(s)
When night fell, we had to hasten to the motor park.
67479.explanation: Hasten means to move or travel hurriedly. Its synonyms include hurry, hurtle, haste, dash, race and bolt.

67482.subject: English Language
67482.question_text:

laugh
67482.explanation: The word 'laugh' rhymes with 'half'. Rhyme scheme refers to the pattern of sounds that repeats at the end of a line or verse.

67485.subject: English Language
67485.question_text: The prisoner finally ........ that he drank to ........ on the night he committed the murder
67485.explanation: The correct answer is 'conceded/excess'. The first blank needs a verb that means 'admit something reluctantly', which is 'conceded'. The second blank needs a noun that means 'an amount of something that is more than necessary', which is 'excess'. The other options do not fit the context of the sentence.

67486.subject: English Language
67486.question_text:
Fill in the gap with the appropriate option:
Children are not allowed in the park ...... dark.
67486.explanation: The phrase "after dark" is an idiomatic expression that means after nightfall or when it becomes dark. In this context, the sentence states that children are not permitted to be in the park during the nighttime.

67487.subject: English Language
67487.question_text:
Fill each gap with the most appropriate option from the list provided.
We had to ..... the group headed by Taiwo.
67487.explanation: "sell up" means to sell all the goods of a debtor to clear the debt, sell off means to clear out (stock) at bargaining prices sell out means to betray for money or reward.

67488.subject: English Language
67488.explanation: The correct answer is 'outstanding'. In this context, the coach is asking for the Bright Rangers to be paid their outstanding salaries. 'Outstanding' in this context means 'yet to be paid' or 'owing'. The other options do not fit into the context of the sentence. 'Left over' implies that there is some salary that has not been used or claimed, which is not the case here. 'Owed' could potentially work, but it is less formal and less precise than 'outstanding'. 'Late' implies that the salaries are delayed, which is not necessarily the case - they could be unpaid for other reasons.

67490.subject: English Language
67490.explanation: The correct answer is 'match bonuses'. In this context, the coach is asking for the Bright Rangers to be paid their outstanding salaries and match bonuses. A 'match bonus' is an extra payment made to players for participating in a particular match, often as a form of incentive. The other options do not fit into the context of the sentence. 'Match payments' and 'match wages' are not standard terms in football, and 'match fees' would typically refer to fees charged to watch a match, not payments made to players.

67492.subject: English Language
67492.explanation: The correct answer is 'spur'. In this context, the coach wants the Bright Rangers to be paid their salaries to 'spur' them to victory. The word 'spur' means to encourage or stimulate into action, which fits perfectly in this context.

67494.subject: English Language
67494.explanation: The correct answer is 'from'. In this context, the Bright Rangers have four points 'from' many matches. The preposition 'from' is used to indicate the source or origin of something, in this case, the source of the points is the many matches they have played.

67499.subject: English Language
67499.explanation: The phrase "stay in the running" means to remain as a viable contender or participant in a competition or race.

67501.subject: English Language
67501.explanation: In the context of the sentence, the coach is talking about the upcoming match against Al - Ahly. The term 'showdown' is often used to refer to a decisive contest or confrontation, which in this case is the match. Therefore, the correct answer is 'Showdown'.

67502.subject: English Language
67502.explanation: In the context of the sentence, the coach is emphasizing the importance of the players being paid their salaries on time to ensure their motivation for the upcoming match. Therefore, the correct answer is 'on time'.

67503.subject: English Language
67503.explanation: In the context of the sentence, the coach is saying that getting paid would be a big morale boost for the team. Therefore, the correct word to fill in the blank is 'Booster'.

67504.subject: English Language
67504.explanation: In the context of the sentence, the coach is saying that the Bright Rangers plan to employ the counter strategy to get a result in Cario. The correct word to fill in the blank is 'Attack'.

67505.subject: English Language
67505.question_text:

It is inconceivable that the cat devoured the cat.
67505.explanation: The correct answer is - credible. The word inconceivable means, that which cannot be believed;credible.

Student

67512.question_text:
Choose the option that has the same consonant sound as the one provided
/θ/

Eating fresh fruits and vegetables is beneficial to one's health while eating processed foods is ......
67523.explanation: Something beneficial is helpful or good to something or someone. The antonyms are detrimental, harmful and unfavourable.

67526.subject: English Language
67526.question_text:
Select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.

The stadium had a capacity crowd in spite of the weather.
67526.explanation: The sentence implies that despite the weather conditions, the stadium was filled to capacity. This suggests that the crowd defied the weather to fill the stadium. Therefore, the option 'The crowd defied the weather to fill the stadium' best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.

options.text: The stadium was not filled because of the weather
The crowd defied the weather to fill the stadium
The crowd loved the weather at the stadium
The weather favoured the crowd at the stadium

67529.subject: English Language
67529.question_text:
Select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.

The conference is biennial.
67529.explanation: The word "biennial" means something that occurs once every two years or once every other year.

options.text: The conference lasts for two years
The conference is held once every other year
The conference is held twice every year
The conference is held twice in two years

Only two ministers survived the recent cabinet reshuffle.

In the recent changes in government, all but two ministers remained alive
In recent changes in government, all but two ministers were sacked
In the recent changes in government, only two ministers were sacked

67537.subject: English Language
67537.question_text:
In this question, choose the option that best completes the gap(s).

The proprietor of our school with his administrator ------------ expected yesterday.
67537.explanation: The correct answer is - was. "with" in the sentence above only introduces the "attachment" of false subjects. Other words that introduce false subjects are: as well as, in conjunction with, alongside, together with etc. Whenever any of these is used in a sentence, it is the noun or pronoun that comes before any of these false subject introducers that will determine the choice of verb to be used.

In Nigeria, it is a crime to plagiarize someone else's work.

What I told you is the gospel truth. This means that the information is
